problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{13}{(3x+2)(2x-3)}=\frac{A}{(3x+2)}+\frac{B}{(2x-3)},
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are real constants, calculate $A+B.$
worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{(3x+2)(2x-3)}=\frac{A}{(3x+2)}+\frac{B}{(2x-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(3x+2)(2x-3)$ gives

$$
13=A(2x-3)+B(3x+2).
$$

For $x=\frac{3}{2}$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}13 & =A(2(\frac{3}{2})-3)+B(3(\frac{3}{2})+2) \\ 13 & =B(\frac{9+4}{2}) \\ B & =\frac{26}{13} \\ B & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=-\frac{2}{3}$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}13 & =A(2(\frac{-2}{3})-3)+B(3(-\frac{2}{3})+2) \\ 13 & =A(\frac{-13}{3}) \\ A & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
A+B=-3+2=-1.
$$
